title: Wave model
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for IB Diploma Physics (status of the source: ai-reviewed-reverified-gate-verified-2026-09-29-awaiting-human-signoff). Terms and clues: C.2#c08 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; C.2#c01 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; C.2#c03 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; C.2#c09 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition. Questions: C.2#q01, C.2#q05, C.2#q02, C.2#q06, C.2#q03, C.2#q07, C.2#q04.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Amplitude
items.clue: The maximum displacement of a particle of the medium from its equilibrium position.

items.label: Travelling (progressive) wave
items.clue: A disturbance that moves through a medium or through space and transfers energy from one place to another.

items.label: Longitudinal wave
items.clue: A travelling wave in which the particles of the medium oscillate parallel to the direction in which the wave transfers energy, producing alternate compressions and rarefactions.

items.label: Wavelength λ
items.clue: The distance between two adjacent points on a wave that are oscillating in phase, e.g. adjacent crests or adjacent compressions; the distance the wave travels in one time period.

questions.stem: Which statement defines a longitudinal wave?

options.text: A wave in which the particles of the medium oscillate parallel to the direction of energy transfer
A wave in which the particles of the medium oscillate perpendicular to the direction of energy transfer
A wave in which the particles of the medium travel along with it, carrying the energy with them
Any wave that travels along the length of a long medium, such as a stretched spring or a rope

questions.explanation: This is the definition. In sound, for example, the air particles move back and forth along the line from source to listener, forming compressions and rarefactions.

questions.stem: A transverse wave travels along a stretched string. Adjacent crests are 1.2 m apart. A graph of displacement y against time t for one point on the string is a sine curve: y = 0 at t = 0, y is a maximum at t = 5 ms, y = 0 at t = 10 ms, y is a minimum at t = 15 ms and y = 0 at t = 20 ms, after which the pattern repeats. What is the wave speed?

options.text: 120 m s⁻¹
60 m s⁻¹

questions.explanation: One full oscillation (maximum, zero, minimum, back to zero) takes T = 20 ms = 0.020 s, and λ = 1.2 m. v = λ/T = 1.2 m ÷ 0.020 s = 60 m s⁻¹.

questions.stem: A transverse wave travels in the +x direction along a stretched rope. At one instant, the graph of the displacement y of the rope (upwards positive) against position x is a sine curve: y = 0 at x = 0, y = +2.0 cm at x = 0.25 m, y = 0 at x = 0.50 m, y = −2.0 cm at x = 0.75 m and y = 0 at x = 1.00 m. How is the point of the rope at x = 0.50 m moving at this instant?

options.text: Downwards (−y), at its maximum speed
Neither way: it is momentarily at rest
In the +x direction, along with the wave
Upwards (+y), at its maximum speed

questions.stem: A vibrator sends a continuous transverse wave along a stretched string. The student increases the amplitude of the vibrator's oscillation but keeps its frequency and the tension in the string the same. What happens to the wave speed and to the wavelength?

options.text: The speed and the wavelength both stay the same, as f and the string are unchanged
Both increase, as a larger amplitude makes the wave move faster along the string
The speed is unchanged; the wavelength is longer, as the wave is now bigger
The speed is unchanged; the wavelength is shorter, as the vibrator now moves faster

questions.explanation: The wave speed is set by the string (its tension and mass per unit length), not by the amplitude. The frequency is unchanged, so λ = v/f is unchanged. Only the energy transferred increases.

questions.stem: A longitudinal wave travels in the +x direction along a slinky spring. Displacements of the coils in the +x direction are positive. At one instant, the graph of displacement s against equilibrium position x is a sine curve: s = 0 at x = 0, s = +3.0 mm at x = 10 cm, s = 0 at x = 20 cm, s = −3.0 mm at x = 30 cm and s = 0 at x = 40 cm. Where, between x = 0 and x = 40 cm, is the centre of a compression?

options.text: At x = 10 cm, where the displacement is greatest and positive
At x = 10 cm and x = 30 cm, where s has its greatest magnitude
At x = 20 cm, where coils on both sides are displaced towards it
At x = 0, 20 cm and 40 cm, where the displacement s is zero

questions.stem: A student measures the wavelength λ of waves on one stretched string at three frequencies f of the vibrator, keeping the tension constant: f = 20 Hz, λ = 1.50 m; f = 40 Hz, λ = 0.75 m; f = 60 Hz, λ = 0.50 m. Which conclusion do the data support?

options.text: The speed rises with frequency, because v = fλ and f was increased each time.
The speed is the same at each frequency, so it does not depend on the frequency.
The speed falls as the frequency rises, because the period rises as frequency does.
No conclusion is possible, as the amplitude, which sets the speed, was not measured.

questions.explanation: fλ = 20 × 1.50 = 40 × 0.75 = 60 × 0.50 = 30 m s⁻¹ in every case. The string sets the speed; raising the frequency shortens the wavelength in inverse proportion.

questions.stem: A student flicks one end of a long, horizontal, stretched rope once, and a single transverse pulse travels along it. A ribbon tied to the rope halfway along moves up and then back down to its original position as the pulse passes. Which statement about the pulse is correct?

options.text: It transferred no energy past the ribbon, since the rope there ended where it started.
It transferred energy along the rope, although the rope had no net displacement.
It transferred energy by carrying sections of the rope along with it to the far end.
It transferred energy, and a bigger flick would have made it travel along faster.
